content: In the very beginning, what did God create?
explanation: The Bible's first sentence tells us God made everything. “In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.” (Genesis 1:1, BSB)

content: On the first day of creation, what did God make just by speaking?
explanation: God spoke, and light appeared. “And God said, “Let there be light,” and there was light.” (Genesis 1:3, BSB)

content: During creation, what name did God give the light?
explanation: God named the light and the darkness. “God called the light “day,” and the darkness He called “night.”” (Genesis 1:5, BSB)

content: On the fourth day of creation, what else did God make besides the two great lights?
explanation: God filled the sky with lights to mark days and seasons. “And He made the stars as well.” (Genesis 1:16, BSB)

content: During creation, in whose image did God create people?
explanation: People are special because they reflect God. “So God created man in His own image” (Genesis 1:27, BSB)

content: At the end of the sixth day, how did God describe everything He had made?
explanation: God was pleased with all He had made. “and indeed, it was very good.” (Genesis 1:31, BSB)

content: After creating everything, what did God do on the seventh day?
explanation: God finished His work and rested. “so on that day He rested from all His work.” (Genesis 2:2, BSB)

content: In the creation story, what did God form the first man from?
explanation: Then God breathed the breath of life into him. “Then the LORD God formed man from the dust of the ground” (Genesis 2:7, BSB)

content: In the creation story, what did God use to make the first woman?
explanation: God made a helper suitable for the man. “And from the rib that the LORD God had taken from the man, He made a woman” (Genesis 2:22, BSB)

content: In the Garden of Eden, which creature tricked the woman?
explanation: The serpent made her doubt what God had said. “Now the serpent was more crafty than any beast of the field” (Genesis 3:1, BSB)
tags: The Garden of Eden and the First Sin

content: In Eden, after the woman ate the forbidden fruit, who did she give some to?
explanation: Adam was with her, and he ate too. “She also gave some to her husband who was with her, and he ate it.” (Genesis 3:6, BSB)
tags: The Garden of Eden and the First Sin

content: After eating the forbidden fruit, what did Adam and Eve sew together to cover themselves?
explanation: Their eyes were opened and they felt ashamed. “so they sewed together fig leaves and made coverings for themselves.” (Genesis 3:7, BSB)
tags: The Garden of Eden and the First Sin

content: When Adam and Eve heard God walking in the garden, what did they do?
explanation: Sin made them afraid to face God. “they hid themselves from the presence of the LORD God among the trees of the garden.” (Genesis 3:8, BSB)
tags: The Garden of Eden and the First Sin

content: After Adam and Eve hid in the garden, what did God call out to Adam?
explanation: God came looking for them. “But the LORD God called out to the man, “Where are you?”” (Genesis 3:9, BSB)
tags: The Garden of Eden and the First Sin

content: When God asked Eve what she had done, whom did she blame?
explanation: Adam blamed Eve, and Eve blamed the serpent. ““The serpent deceived me,” she replied, “and I ate.”” (Genesis 3:13, BSB)
tags: The Garden of Eden and the First Sin

content: After the first sin, what name did Adam give his wife?
explanation: She would be the mother of all the living. “And Adam named his wife Eve” (Genesis 3:20, BSB)
tags: The Garden of Eden and the First Sin

content: After sending Adam and Eve out of Eden, what did God place to guard the tree of life?
explanation: The way back to the tree of life was closed. “and stationed cherubim on the east side of the Garden of Eden, along with a whirling sword of flame” (Genesis 3:24, BSB)
tags: The Garden of Eden and the First Sin

content: What job did Abel, Adam's son, have?
explanation: Abel was a shepherd; his brother Cain was a farmer. “Now Abel was a keeper of sheep” (Genesis 4:2, BSB)

content: What job did Cain, Adam's son, have?
explanation: Cain was a farmer; his brother Abel was a shepherd. “while Cain was a tiller of the soil.” (Genesis 4:2, BSB)

content: When Cain and Abel brought offerings, whose offering did God look on with favor?
explanation: Abel brought the best of his flock. “And the LORD looked with favor on Abel and his offering” (Genesis 4:4, BSB)

content: How did Cain feel when God did not accept his offering?
explanation: His anger led him to sin. “So Cain became very angry, and his countenance fell.” (Genesis 4:5, BSB)

content: Out in the field, what did Cain do to his brother Abel?
explanation: This was the first murder in the Bible. “Cain rose up against his brother Abel and killed him.” (Genesis 4:8, BSB)

content: When God asked Cain where Abel was, what did Cain answer?
explanation: Cain tried to hide what he had done. ““Am I my brother’s keeper?”” (Genesis 4:9, BSB)

content: After Cain killed Abel, what did God put on Cain to protect him?
explanation: The mark kept others from killing Cain. “And the LORD placed a mark on Cain” (Genesis 4:15, BSB)

content: When the world was full of evil, who found favor in the eyes of the LORD?
explanation: Noah walked with God in a wicked world. “Noah, however, found favor in the eyes of the LORD.” (Genesis 6:8, BSB)

content: Before the flood, how many sons did Noah have?
explanation: His sons were Shem, Ham, and Japheth. “And Noah had three sons: Shem, Ham, and Japheth.” (Genesis 6:10, BSB)

content: Before the flood, what did God tell Noah to build?
explanation: The ark would keep Noah's family and the animals alive. “Make for yourself an ark of gopher wood” (Genesis 6:14, BSB)

content: What kind of animal pairs did God tell Noah to bring into the ark?
explanation: The animals would fill the earth again after the flood. “you are to bring two of every living creature into the ark—male and female” (Genesis 6:19, BSB)

content: In Noah's flood, how long did the rain fall?
explanation: The waters covered even the high mountains. “And the rain fell upon the earth for forty days and forty nights.” (Genesis 7:12, BSB)

content: When the floodwaters went down, where did Noah's ark come to rest?
explanation: The ark settled as the waters slowly went down. “the ark came to rest on the mountains of Ararat.” (Genesis 8:4, BSB)

content: After the flood, what was the first bird Noah sent out of the ark?
explanation: Later Noah sent out a dove. “and sent out a raven.” (Genesis 8:7, BSB)

content: After the flood, what did the dove bring back to Noah in her beak?
explanation: Noah knew the waters had gone down. “the dove returned to him in the evening with a freshly plucked olive leaf in her beak.” (Genesis 8:11, BSB)

content: When Noah came out of the ark, what did he build?
explanation: Noah thanked God with burnt offerings. “Then Noah built an altar to the LORD.” (Genesis 8:20, BSB)

content: After the flood, what sign of His promise did God set in the clouds?
explanation: God promised never again to destroy the earth by a flood. “I have set My rainbow in the clouds” (Genesis 9:13, BSB)

content: Before the Tower of Babel, how many languages did the whole world speak?
explanation: Everyone could understand everyone else. “Now the whole world had one language and a common form of speech.” (Genesis 11:1, BSB)

content: When people built the Tower of Babel, what did they use instead of stone?
explanation: They baked bricks to build their city and tower. “So they used brick instead of stone” (Genesis 11:3, BSB)

content: Why did the people at Babel want a tower that reached to the heavens?
options: To make a name for themselves
explanation: They wanted fame and to stay together in one place. “that we may make a name for ourselves” (Genesis 11:4, BSB)

content: At the Tower of Babel, what did God do to the people's language?
explanation: They could no longer understand one another. “Come, let Us go down and confuse their language” (Genesis 11:7, BSB)

content: After God confused their language, what did the builders at Babel stop doing?
explanation: God scattered them over all the earth. “and they stopped building the city.” (Genesis 11:8, BSB)

content: What was the city with the unfinished tower called?
explanation: There the LORD confused the language of the whole world. “That is why it is called Babel” (Genesis 11:9, BSB)

content: In the Garden of Eden, which two trees stood in the middle of the garden?
options: A fig tree and a vine
Tree of life, tree of knowledge
explanation: God told Adam not to eat from the tree of knowledge. “And in the middle of the garden were the tree of life and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.” (Genesis 2:9, BSB)

content: Why did God put the first man in the Garden of Eden?
explanation: From the start, God gave people good work to do. “and placed him in the Garden of Eden to cultivate and keep it.” (Genesis 2:15, BSB)

content: In the Garden of Eden, what did God say was not good?
options: For the garden to be empty
For the man to be alone
For the animals to be wild
explanation: So God made a suitable helper for him. “It is not good for the man to be alone.” (Genesis 2:18, BSB)

content: In the Garden of Eden, who gave names to all the animals?
explanation: God brought the animals to the man to name them. “The man gave names to all the livestock” (Genesis 2:20, BSB)

content: After the first sin, God told the serpent the woman's offspring would crush what?
explanation: This is the first promise that evil would be defeated. “He will crush your head, and you will strike his heel.” (Genesis 3:15, BSB)

content: After the first sin, God told Adam he would one day return to what?
explanation: Adam was made from the ground. “For dust you are, and to dust you shall return.” (Genesis 3:19, BSB)

content: After the first sin, what did God make to clothe Adam and Eve?
explanation: God cared for them even after they sinned. “And the LORD God made garments of skin for Adam and his wife, and He clothed them.” (Genesis 3:21, BSB)

content: When Cain was angry, God warned him that something was crouching at his door. What?
explanation: God told Cain he must master it. “sin is crouching at your door” (Genesis 4:7, BSB)

content: After killing Abel, where did Cain go to live?
explanation: Nod was east of Eden. “and settled in the land of Nod, east of Eden.” (Genesis 4:16, BSB)

content: After Abel died, what did Adam and Eve name their next son?
explanation: Eve said God had given her another child in place of Abel. “she gave birth to a son and named him Seth” (Genesis 4:25, BSB)

content: In the family line from Adam to Noah, who lived a total of 969 years?
explanation: He is the oldest person named in the Bible. “So Methuselah lived a total of 969 years” (Genesis 5:27, BSB)

content: Before the flood, which man walked with God and then was taken away by God?
explanation: Enoch did not die like the others in his family line. “Enoch walked with God, and then he was no more, because God had taken him away.” (Genesis 5:24, BSB)

content: What kind of wood did God tell Noah to use for the ark?
explanation: God gave Noah exact building instructions. “Make for yourself an ark of gopher wood” (Genesis 6:14, BSB)

content: How does Genesis describe Noah's character before the flood?
explanation: Noah walked with God. “Noah was a righteous man, blameless in his generation” (Genesis 6:9, BSB)

content: After the flood, God promised that as long as the earth lasts, what would never stop?
options: Seedtime and harvest, day and night
explanation: God promised a steady world after the flood. “seedtime and harvest, cold and heat, summer and winter, day and night shall never cease.” (Genesis 8:22, BSB)

content: How long did God tell Noah to make the ark?
explanation: It was also 50 cubits wide and 30 cubits high. “The ark is to be 300 cubits long” (Genesis 6:15, BSB)

content: In Noah's flood, how long did the waters prevail on the earth?
explanation: The rain lasted forty days, but the water stayed much longer. “And the waters prevailed upon the earth for 150 days.” (Genesis 7:24, BSB)

content: How many pairs of each kind of clean animal did Noah take into the ark?
explanation: Unclean animals came in one pair each. “You are to take with you seven pairs of every kind of clean animal” (Genesis 7:2, BSB)

content: How old was Noah when the floodwaters burst forth?
explanation: It happened on the seventeenth day of the second month. “In the six hundredth year of Noah’s life” (Genesis 7:11, BSB)

content: Where did people settle before building the Tower of Babel?
options: A plain in the land of Shinar
explanation: They journeyed eastward and settled there. “they found a plain in the land of Shinar and settled there.” (Genesis 11:2, BSB)

content: After whom did Cain name the city he built?
explanation: This Enoch is not the Enoch who walked with God. “Then Cain built a city and named it after his son Enoch.” (Genesis 4:17, BSB)

content: When building at Babel, what did people use instead of mortar?
explanation: They also used brick instead of stone. “and tar instead of mortar.” (Genesis 11:3, BSB)

content: In the family line from Adam to Noah, how many years did Enoch live in all?
explanation: Then God took him away. “So Enoch lived a total of 365 years.” (Genesis 5:23, BSB)

content: When God called Abram, what did He tell him to leave behind?
explanation: God asked Abram to go to a land He would show him. “Leave your country, your kindred, and your father’s household” (Genesis 12:1, BSB)

content: When God called Abram, what did He promise to make him into?
explanation: God also promised to bless him. “I will make you into a great nation” (Genesis 12:2, BSB)

content: When Abram obeyed God's call and left Haran, which nephew went with him?
explanation: Abram took Sarai and Lot with him. “and Lot went with him.” (Genesis 12:4, BSB)

content: When Abram obeyed God's call, which land did he set out for?
explanation: This was the land God promised to his offspring. “and set out for the land of Canaan.” (Genesis 12:5, BSB)

content: When God appeared to Abram in Canaan, what did Abram build there?
explanation: Abram worshiped the God who had spoken to him. “So Abram built an altar there to the LORD” (Genesis 12:7, BSB)

content: When God called Abram, who did He say would be blessed through him?
options: All the families of the earth
explanation: God's plan for Abram reached the whole world. “and all the families of the earth will be blessed through you.” (Genesis 12:3, BSB)

content: When God gave childless Abram a promise at night, what did He tell him to count?
explanation: Abram's offspring would be as many as the stars. “Now look to the heavens and count the stars, if you are able.” (Genesis 15:5, BSB)
tags: The Promise: Offspring Like the Stars

content: In a vision, God told Abram, “Do not be afraid. I am your…” what?
explanation: God promised to protect Abram and be his reward. “I am your shield, your very great reward.” (Genesis 15:1, BSB)
tags: The Promise: Offspring Like the Stars

content: When God promised Abram offspring like the stars, how did Abram respond?
explanation: God counted Abram's faith as righteousness. “Abram believed the LORD, and it was credited to him as righteousness.” (Genesis 15:6, BSB)
tags: The Promise: Offspring Like the Stars

content: Before God's promise of offspring like the stars, what was Abram worried about?
explanation: A servant was going to inherit everything. “since I remain childless” (Genesis 15:2, BSB)
tags: The Promise: Offspring Like the Stars

content: God promised childless Abram that his heir would be whom?
explanation: God promised Abram a child of his own. “but one who comes from your own body will be your heir.” (Genesis 15:4, BSB)
tags: The Promise: Offspring Like the Stars

content: When two angels came to Sodom in the evening, who was sitting in the city gateway?
explanation: Lot got up to meet them and bowed down. “and Lot was sitting in the gateway of the city.” (Genesis 19:1, BSB)

content: At daybreak in Sodom, what did the angels urge Lot to do?
options: Fight the men of the city
explanation: The city was about to be destroyed. “Take your wife and your two daughters who are here” (Genesis 19:15, BSB)

content: As Lot's family fled Sodom, what did the angels tell them not to do?
explanation: They had to run for their lives to the mountains. “Do not look back” (Genesis 19:17, BSB)

content: What did the LORD rain down on Sodom and Gomorrah?
explanation: God judged the wicked cities. “Then the LORD rained down sulfur and fire on Sodom and Gomorrah” (Genesis 19:24, BSB)

content: When Lot's wife looked back at Sodom, what did she become?
explanation: She did not obey the angels' warning. “But Lot’s wife looked back, and she became a pillar of salt.” (Genesis 19:26, BSB)

content: When Lot hesitated to leave Sodom, what did the angels do?
options: Took their hands and led them out
explanation: The LORD had compassion on Lot's family. “the men grabbed his hand and the hands of his wife and his two daughters.” (Genesis 19:16, BSB)

content: What did Abraham name the son that Sarah bore him in their old age?
explanation: God kept His promise to Abraham and Sarah. “And Abraham gave the name Isaac to the son Sarah bore to him.” (Genesis 21:3, BSB)

content: How old was Abraham when his son Isaac was born?
explanation: Nothing is too hard for the LORD. “Abraham was a hundred years old when his son Isaac was born to him.” (Genesis 21:5, BSB)

content: After Isaac was born, what did Sarah say God had made her do?
explanation: Her laugh of doubt became a laugh of joy. “God has made me laugh” (Genesis 21:6, BSB)

content: What did Abraham hold on the day his son Isaac was weaned?
explanation: The family celebrated the promised child. “and Abraham held a great feast on the day Isaac was weaned.” (Genesis 21:8, BSB)

content: When Hagar and her boy ran out of water in the wilderness, what did God show her?
explanation: God heard the boy's voice and cared for them. “Then God opened her eyes, and she saw a well of water.” (Genesis 21:19, BSB)

content: When was Isaac born to Abraham and Sarah?
options: At the very time God promised
explanation: God did exactly what He had said. “at the very time God had promised.” (Genesis 21:2, BSB)

content: When God tested Abraham, whom did He tell him to offer?
explanation: God was testing Abraham's trust. “your only son Isaac, whom you love” (Genesis 22:2, BSB)

content: When God tested Abraham, which land did He send him to?
explanation: God would show him one of the mountains there. “and go to the land of Moriah.” (Genesis 22:2, BSB)

content: As Abraham and Isaac walked up the mountain, what did Isaac carry?
explanation: Abraham carried the fire and the knife. “Abraham took the wood for the burnt offering and placed it on his son Isaac.” (Genesis 22:6, BSB)

content: On the way up the mountain, what did Isaac ask his father Abraham?
explanation: Isaac saw the fire and wood but no lamb. “but where is the lamb for the burnt offering?” (Genesis 22:7, BSB)

content: When Isaac asked where the lamb was, what did Abraham answer?
explanation: Abraham trusted God to provide. “God Himself will provide the lamb for the burnt offering, my son.” (Genesis 22:8, BSB)

content: Just as Abraham took the knife on the mountain, who called out to stop him?
explanation: Abraham had shown that he feared God. “Just then the angel of the LORD called out to him from heaven” (Genesis 22:11, BSB)

content: On the mountain, what did Abraham offer in place of his son Isaac?
options: A ram caught in a thicket
explanation: God provided a ram, caught by its horns. “and saw behind him a ram in a thicket, caught by its horns.” (Genesis 22:13, BSB)

content: In his old age, Abraham sent his servant to find a wife for whom?
explanation: The wife was to come from Abraham's own relatives. “to take a wife for my son Isaac.” (Genesis 24:4, BSB)

content: What animals did Abraham's servant take on his trip to find a wife for Isaac?
explanation: He also took many good gifts from his master. “Then the servant took ten of his master’s camels” (Genesis 24:10, BSB)

content: Looking for a wife for Isaac, where did Abraham's servant stop his camels to pray?
options: By a well outside the town
explanation: It was the time women came to draw water. “he made the camels kneel down near the well outside the town” (Genesis 24:11, BSB)

content: While Abraham's servant was still praying at the well, who came out with her jar?
explanation: God answered before he finished praying. “Before the servant had finished praying, Rebekah came out with her jar on her shoulder.” (Genesis 24:15, BSB)

content: At the well, what did Rebekah offer to do for the camels of Abraham's servant?
explanation: This was the sign the servant had prayed for. “I will also draw water for your camels, until they have had enough to drink.” (Genesis 24:19, BSB)

content: When her family asked Rebekah if she would go with Abraham's servant to marry Isaac, what did she say?
explanation: Rebekah chose to go to Isaac. ““I will go,” she replied.” (Genesis 24:58, BSB)

content: How did Isaac feel about Rebekah after he married her?
explanation: She comforted him after his mother's death. “And Isaac loved her and was comforted after his mother’s death.” (Genesis 24:67, BSB)

content: When Rebekah, Isaac's wife, gave birth, what was special about her children?
explanation: The twins were Esau and Jacob. “there were indeed twins in her womb.” (Genesis 25:24, BSB)

content: Which of Isaac's twins was born first, red and hairy?
explanation: He was covered with hair like a fur coat. “The first one came out red, covered with hair like a fur coat; so they named him Esau.” (Genesis 25:25, BSB)

content: When Jacob was born right after his twin, what was he holding on to?
explanation: That is how he got the name Jacob. “his brother came out grasping Esau’s heel” (Genesis 25:26, BSB)

content: When Isaac's twins grew up, what kind of man was Esau?
explanation: Jacob was the quiet one who stayed at home. “Esau became a skillful hunter” (Genesis 25:27, BSB)

content: One day Esau came in from the field very hungry. What was Jacob cooking?
explanation: Esau begged for some of the red stew. “while Jacob was cooking some stew” (Genesis 25:29, BSB)

content: What did Jacob ask Esau to sell him for a bowl of stew?
explanation: Esau traded something precious for one meal. ““First sell me your birthright,” Jacob replied.” (Genesis 25:31, BSB)

content: Which of the twin brothers did their mother Rebekah love?
explanation: Isaac loved Esau, but Rebekah loved Jacob. “but Rebekah loved Jacob.” (Genesis 25:28, BSB)

content: How old was Abram when he left Haran at God's call?
explanation: Abram obeyed God even in old age. “Abram was seventy-five years old when he left Haran.” (Genesis 12:4, BSB)

content: When a severe famine struck Canaan, where did Abram go to live for a while?
explanation: There was not enough food in the land. “So Abram went down to Egypt to live there for a while because the famine was severe.” (Genesis 12:10, BSB)

content: When Abram and Lot separated, which land did Lot choose for himself?
explanation: It looked well watered like the garden of the LORD. “So Lot chose the whole plain of the Jordan for himself” (Genesis 13:11, BSB)

content: After separating from Abram, Lot pitched his tent toward which city?
explanation: Lot moved near the wicked city of Sodom. “and pitched his tent toward Sodom.” (Genesis 13:12, BSB)

content: Which king of Salem brought bread and wine to Abram?
explanation: He was priest of God Most High. “Then Melchizedek king of Salem brought out bread and wine” (Genesis 14:18, BSB)

content: After Melchizedek blessed him, what did Abram give Melchizedek?
explanation: Abram honored the priest of God Most High. “Then Abram gave Melchizedek a tenth of everything.” (Genesis 14:20, BSB)

content: What was the name of Sarai's Egyptian maidservant?
explanation: Sarai gave Hagar to Abram because she had no children. “but she had an Egyptian maidservant named Hagar.” (Genesis 16:1, BSB)

content: What did Abram name the son that Hagar bore him?
explanation: Ishmael was born before Isaac. “and Abram gave the name Ishmael to the son she had borne.” (Genesis 16:15, BSB)

content: When God made His covenant with Abram, what new name did He give him?
explanation: His new name meant he would be a father of many nations. “but your name will be Abraham, for I have made you a father of many nations.” (Genesis 17:5, BSB)

content: When God renamed Abraham, what new name did He give Abraham's wife Sarai?
explanation: God promised she would be the mother of nations. “for her name is to be Sarah.” (Genesis 17:15, BSB)

content: When God appeared to Abram at age ninety-nine, what name did He call Himself?
explanation: God told Abram to walk before Him and be blameless. “I am God Almighty.” (Genesis 17:1, BSB)

content: By the Oaks of Mamre, how many men did Abraham see standing near his tent?
explanation: Abraham ran to welcome his visitors. “And Abraham looked up and saw three men standing nearby.” (Genesis 18:2, BSB)

content: When Sarah overheard that she would have a son in her old age, what did she do?
explanation: She thought she was too old. “So she laughed to herself” (Genesis 18:12, BSB)

content: When Sarah laughed at the promise of a son, what did the LORD ask Abraham?
options: Is anything too difficult for the LORD?
explanation: God promised Sarah would have a son in about a year. “Is anything too difficult for the LORD?” (Genesis 18:14, BSB)

content: When Abraham pleaded for Sodom, what was the smallest number of righteous people he asked about?
explanation: God said He would spare the city for ten. “Suppose ten are found there?” (Genesis 18:32, BSB)

content: What did Abraham name the mountain where God provided a ram in Isaac's place?
explanation: God had provided the sacrifice. “And Abraham called that place The LORD Will Provide.” (Genesis 22:14, BSB)

content: After Abraham's test on the mountain, God promised to multiply his descendants like what?
explanation: Abraham had not held back his only son. “I will multiply your descendants like the stars in the sky and the sand on the seashore.” (Genesis 22:17, BSB)

content: What was the name of Rebekah's brother, who rushed out to meet Abraham's servant?
explanation: Bethuel was her father; Laban was her brother. “Now Rebekah had a brother named Laban” (Genesis 24:29, BSB)

content: What was Isaac doing in the field when Rebekah's camels came into view?
explanation: He looked up and saw the camels approaching. “Isaac went out to the field to meditate” (Genesis 24:63, BSB)

content: Because he asked for the red stew, what other name was Esau given?
explanation: Edom sounds like the word for red. “(That is why he was also called Edom.)” (Genesis 25:30, BSB)

content: What did Jacob give Esau in exchange for his birthright?
explanation: Esau ate, drank, and went away. “Then Jacob gave some bread and lentil stew to Esau” (Genesis 25:34, BSB)

content: Before Rebekah's twins were born, what did God say about the older and the younger?
options: The younger will serve the older
They will live apart in peace
The older will serve the younger
explanation: God told her two nations were in her womb. “and the older will serve the younger.” (Genesis 25:23, BSB)

content: Where did Hagar wander with her son after Abraham sent them away?
explanation: Abraham gave her bread and a skin of water. “She left and wandered in the Wilderness of Beersheba.” (Genesis 21:14, BSB)

content: In Canaan, Abram traveled as far as the Oak of Moreh at which place?
explanation: There the LORD appeared to him. “as far as the site of the Oak of Moreh at Shechem.” (Genesis 12:6, BSB)

content: In Canaan, Abram pitched his tent with Bethel to the west and which town to the east?
explanation: There he built another altar to the LORD. “with Bethel to the west and Ai to the east.” (Genesis 12:8, BSB)

content: Before Isaac was born, who did Abram say would inherit his house?
explanation: Abram had no child of his own yet. “and the heir of my house is Eliezer of Damascus?” (Genesis 15:2, BSB)

content: How long had Abram lived in Canaan when Sarai gave him Hagar as a wife?
explanation: Sarai still had no children. “So after he had lived in Canaan for ten years” (Genesis 16:3, BSB)

content: At what age did Abraham circumcise his son Isaac?
explanation: Abraham did as God had commanded him. “When his son Isaac was eight days old, Abraham circumcised him” (Genesis 21:4, BSB)

content: How old was Abraham's wife Sarah when she died?
explanation: She died in Hebron in the land of Canaan. “Now Sarah lived to be 127 years old.” (Genesis 23:1, BSB)

content: Where did Abraham bury his wife Sarah?
explanation: The cave was near Mamre, that is, Hebron. “Abraham buried his wife Sarah in the cave of the field at Machpelah near Mamre” (Genesis 23:19, BSB)

content: How many years did Abraham live in all?
explanation: He died old and contented. “Abraham lived a total of 175 years.” (Genesis 25:7, BSB)

content: How old was Isaac when he married Rebekah?
explanation: Rebekah was the sister of Laban the Aramean. “and Isaac was forty years old when he married Rebekah” (Genesis 25:20, BSB)

content: How old was Isaac when his twin sons Esau and Jacob were born?
explanation: Isaac had prayed for his wife because she was barren. “And Isaac was sixty years old when the twins were born.” (Genesis 25:26, BSB)

content: Looking for a wife for Isaac, Abraham's servant set out for Nahor's hometown in which region?
explanation: Abraham's relatives lived there. “And he set out for Nahor’s hometown in Aram-naharaim.” (Genesis 24:10, BSB)

content: When God promised Abraham a son by Sarah, how old did Abraham say Sarah was?
explanation: Abraham himself was nearly a hundred. “Can Sarah give birth at the age of ninety?” (Genesis 17:17, BSB)

content: On his way to Haran, what did Jacob use as a pillow when he slept?
explanation: He stopped for the night because the sun had set. “And taking one of the stones from that place, he put it under his head and lay down to sleep.” (Genesis 28:11, BSB)

content: Sleeping on his way to Haran, what did Jacob dream about?
explanation: The ladder rested on the earth and reached heaven. “And Jacob had a dream about a ladder that rested on the earth with its top reaching up to heaven” (Genesis 28:12, BSB)

content: In Jacob's dream on the way to Haran, who was going up and down the ladder?
explanation: At the top stood the LORD Himself. “and God’s angels were going up and down the ladder.” (Genesis 28:12, BSB)

content: In Jacob's ladder dream, what did God promise to do wherever Jacob went?
explanation: God promised to bring Jacob back to the land. “Look, I am with you, and I will watch over you wherever you go” (Genesis 28:15, BSB)

content: When Jacob woke from his ladder dream, what did he say about that place?
options: Surely the LORD is in this place
explanation: Jacob had not known God was there. “Surely the LORD is in this place, and I was unaware of it.” (Genesis 28:16, BSB)

content: After his ladder dream, what did Jacob do with the stone he had slept on?
options: Used it to build a house
Set it up as a pillar
explanation: He poured oil on it to mark the place. “and he set it up as a pillar. He poured oil on top of it” (Genesis 28:18, BSB)

content: What name did Jacob give the place where he dreamed of the ladder?
explanation: Bethel means house of God. “and he called that place Bethel” (Genesis 28:19, BSB)

content: The night before Jacob met Esau again, what happened when Jacob was left alone?
explanation: They wrestled through the night. “So Jacob was left all alone, and there a man wrestled with him until daybreak.” (Genesis 32:24, BSB)

content: On the night before meeting Esau, how long did the man wrestle with Jacob?
explanation: Jacob would not give up. “a man wrestled with him until daybreak.” (Genesis 32:24, BSB)

content: When the man he wrestled said, “Let me go,” what did Jacob answer?
explanation: Jacob wanted God's blessing. “I will not let you go unless you bless me.” (Genesis 32:26, BSB)

content: After wrestling all night, what new name was Jacob given?
explanation: He had struggled with God and with men and prevailed. “Your name will no longer be Jacob, but Israel” (Genesis 32:28, BSB)

content: After wrestling with the man until daybreak, how did Jacob walk?
explanation: The man had struck his hip. “and he was limping because of his hip.” (Genesis 32:31, BSB)

content: Why did Jacob name the place where he wrestled Peniel?
options: He had seen God face to face
explanation: Jacob was amazed his life was spared. “Indeed, I have seen God face to face, and yet my life was spared.” (Genesis 32:30, BSB)

content: When Isaac was old and ready to bless his son, what was wrong with his eyes?
options: They were too weak to see
explanation: Because he could not see, Jacob could trick him. “When Isaac was old and his eyes were so weak that he could no longer see” (Genesis 27:1, BSB)

content: When old Isaac planned to bless Esau, what did he first ask Esau to do?
explanation: Isaac wanted a tasty meal before giving the blessing. “go out into the field to hunt some game for me.” (Genesis 27:3, BSB)

content: To trick blind Isaac, what did Rebekah put on Jacob's hands and neck?
explanation: Esau was hairy, and Jacob was smooth. “She also put the skins of the young goats on his hands and on the smooth part of his neck.” (Genesis 27:16, BSB)

content: When blind Isaac touched Jacob, what did he say about the voice and the hands?
explanation: Isaac was unsure but blessed Jacob anyway. “The voice is the voice of Jacob, but the hands are the hands of Esau.” (Genesis 27:22, BSB)

content: When Esau planned to kill Jacob over the stolen blessing, where did Rebekah tell Jacob to flee?
options: To her brother Laban in Haran
explanation: She wanted Jacob safe until Esau calmed down. “flee at once to my brother Laban in Haran.” (Genesis 27:43, BSB)

content: When Jacob reached Haran, who arrived at the well with her father's sheep?
explanation: Rachel was a shepherdess. “Rachel arrived with her father’s sheep, for she was a shepherdess.” (Genesis 29:9, BSB)

content: When Jacob first saw Rachel at the well in Haran, what did he do for her?
options: Rolled the stone away, watered her sheep
explanation: Rachel was the daughter of his uncle Laban. “he went up and rolled the stone away from the mouth of the well and watered his uncle’s sheep.” (Genesis 29:10, BSB)

content: How many years did Jacob offer to work for Laban to marry Rachel?
explanation: Jacob loved Rachel. “I will serve you seven years for your younger daughter Rachel.” (Genesis 29:18, BSB)

content: How did Jacob's seven years of work for Rachel feel to him?
explanation: His love for her made the time fly. “yet it seemed but a few days because of his love for her.” (Genesis 29:20, BSB)

content: After working seven years for Rachel, whom did Jacob find he had married?
explanation: Laban had tricked Jacob. “When morning came, there was Leah!” (Genesis 29:25, BSB)

content: What were the names of Laban's two daughters?
explanation: Leah was older and Rachel was younger. “the older was named Leah, and the younger was named Rachel.” (Genesis 29:16, BSB)

content: What did Rachel name her first son?
explanation: God remembered Rachel and gave her a son. “She named him Joseph” (Genesis 30:24, BSB)

content: When Jacob returned home, how many men were coming with Esau to meet him?
explanation: Jacob was greatly afraid. “he and four hundred men with him.” (Genesis 32:6, BSB)

content: When Esau finally met Jacob again after many years, what did Esau do?
explanation: The brothers wept together. “Esau, however, ran to him and embraced him” (Genesis 33:4, BSB)

content: As Jacob approached Esau after many years apart, how many times did he bow to the ground?
explanation: Jacob came humbly to his brother. “and bowed to the ground seven times as he approached his brother.” (Genesis 33:3, BSB)

content: As Rachel was dying in childbirth, what name did Jacob give her newborn son?
explanation: Rachel had named him Ben-oni. “But his father called him Benjamin.” (Genesis 35:18, BSB)

content: How many sons did Jacob have in all?
explanation: They became the twelve tribes of Israel. “Jacob had twelve sons:” (Genesis 35:22, BSB)

content: What did Isaac name the well that no one quarreled over?
explanation: Isaac said the LORD had made room for them. “He named it Rehoboth” (Genesis 26:22, BSB)

content: Before Jacob named it Bethel, what was that city called?
explanation: Jacob renamed it after his ladder dream. “though previously the city had been named Luz.” (Genesis 28:19, BSB)

content: At Bethel, how much of all God gave him did Jacob vow to give back?
explanation: Jacob made a vow after his dream. “and of all that You give me I will surely give You a tenth.” (Genesis 28:22, BSB)

content: Which servant girl did Laban give to his daughter Leah as her maidservant?
explanation: Bilhah was given to Rachel. “And Laban gave his servant girl Zilpah to his daughter Leah as her maidservant.” (Genesis 29:24, BSB)

content: How many years in all did Jacob serve in Laban's household?
explanation: Fourteen years for his wives and six for his flocks. “Thus for twenty years I have served in your household” (Genesis 31:41, BSB)

content: Jacob complained that his uncle Laban had changed his wages how many times?
explanation: Laban kept cheating Jacob. “and you have changed my wages ten times!” (Genesis 31:41, BSB)

content: When angels met Jacob on his way home, what did he name that place?
explanation: He called it the camp of God. “So he named that place Mahanaim.” (Genesis 32:2, BSB)

content: The night before meeting Esau, which stream did Jacob's family cross?
explanation: Then Jacob was left alone. “and crossed the ford of the Jabbok.” (Genesis 32:22, BSB)

content: Where was Jacob's wife Rachel buried?
explanation: Ephrath is Bethlehem. “So Rachel died and was buried on the way to Ephrath (that is, Bethlehem).” (Genesis 35:19, BSB)

content: Who was Jacob's firstborn son?
explanation: Reuben was Leah's first son. “The sons of Leah were Reuben the firstborn of Jacob” (Genesis 35:23, BSB)

content: What special gift did Jacob make for his son Joseph?
explanation: Jacob loved Joseph more than his other sons. “so he made him a robe of many colors.” (Genesis 37:3, BSB)

content: Why did Joseph's brothers hate him?
explanation: They could not even speak a kind word to him. “When Joseph’s brothers saw that their father loved him more than any of them, they hated him” (Genesis 37:4, BSB)

content: In young Joseph's first dream, what bowed down to his sheaf of grain?
explanation: His brothers hated him even more after this dream. “while your sheaves gathered around and bowed down to mine.” (Genesis 37:7, BSB)

content: In young Joseph's second dream, what was bowing down to him?
options: The sun, moon, and eleven stars
explanation: Even his father wondered about this dream. “the sun and moon and eleven stars were bowing down to me.” (Genesis 37:9, BSB)

content: When Joseph's brothers saw him coming in the fields, what did they call him?
explanation: They were angry about his dreams. ““Here comes that dreamer!” they said to one another.” (Genesis 37:19, BSB)

content: After taking his colorful robe, where did Joseph's brothers throw him?
explanation: The pit had no water in it. “and they took him and threw him into the pit. Now the pit was empty, with no water in it.” (Genesis 37:24, BSB)

content: Who did Joseph's jealous brothers sell him to?
explanation: The traders took Joseph to Egypt. “and sold him for twenty shekels of silver to the Ishmaelites, who took him to Egypt.” (Genesis 37:28, BSB)

content: After selling Joseph, what did his brothers dip his robe in to fool their father?
explanation: They wanted Jacob to think an animal had killed Joseph. “slaughtered a young goat, and dipped the robe in its blood.” (Genesis 37:31, BSB)

content: In Pharaoh's first dream, what came up out of the Nile?
explanation: Then seven thin cows came up after them. “when seven cows, sleek and well-fed, came up from the river” (Genesis 41:2, BSB)

content: In Pharaoh's dream by the Nile, what did the thin cows do to the fat cows?
explanation: Then Pharaoh woke up troubled. “And the cows that were sickly and thin devoured the seven sleek, well-fed cows.” (Genesis 41:4, BSB)

content: When Pharaoh asked Joseph to explain his dream, who did Joseph say would give the answer?
explanation: Joseph gave God the credit. “but God will give Pharaoh a sound answer.” (Genesis 41:16, BSB)

content: Joseph said Pharaoh's dreams meant seven years of plenty followed by what?
explanation: Egypt needed to store food during the good years. “but seven years of famine will follow them.” (Genesis 41:30, BSB)

content: After Joseph explained the dreams, what did Pharaoh put him in charge of?
explanation: Pharaoh saw that God's Spirit was in Joseph. “I hereby place you over all the land of Egypt.” (Genesis 41:41, BSB)

content: When Pharaoh put Joseph in charge of Egypt, what did he put on Joseph's finger?
explanation: The ring showed Joseph had Pharaoh's authority. “Then Pharaoh removed the signet ring from his finger, put it on Joseph’s finger” (Genesis 41:42, BSB)

content: During the great famine, why did every nation come to Joseph in Egypt?
explanation: Joseph had stored grain during the good years. “And every nation came to Joseph in Egypt to buy grain” (Genesis 41:57, BSB)

content: When Joseph finally told his brothers in Egypt who he was, what did he say?
explanation: He also asked if his father was still alive. “Joseph said to his brothers, “I am Joseph! Is my father still alive?”” (Genesis 45:3, BSB)
tags: Joseph Makes Himself Known to His Brothers

content: When Joseph revealed who he was, how did his brothers feel?
explanation: They could not even answer him. “because they were terrified in his presence.” (Genesis 45:3, BSB)
tags: Joseph Makes Himself Known to His Brothers

content: When Joseph made himself known to his brothers, how loudly did he weep?
explanation: Even Pharaoh's household heard about it. “But he wept so loudly that the Egyptians heard him” (Genesis 45:2, BSB)
tags: Joseph Makes Himself Known to His Brothers

content: Joseph told his brothers that God sent him to Egypt ahead of them for what reason?
explanation: Joseph saw God's plan in all that happened. “because it was to save lives that God sent me before you.” (Genesis 45:5, BSB)
tags: Joseph Makes Himself Known to His Brothers

content: Joseph told his brothers who had really sent him to Egypt. Who?
explanation: God had made him ruler over Egypt. “Therefore it was not you who sent me here, but God” (Genesis 45:8, BSB)
tags: Joseph Makes Himself Known to His Brothers

content: In which region of Egypt did Joseph invite his family to settle?
explanation: There they could be near Joseph. “You shall settle in the land of Goshen and be near me” (Genesis 45:10, BSB)
tags: Joseph Makes Himself Known to His Brothers

content: When old Jacob heard that Joseph was alive, what did he decide?
options: To go see him before he died
explanation: Jacob had mourned Joseph for many years. “My son Joseph is still alive! I will go to see him before I die.” (Genesis 45:28, BSB)
tags: Joseph Makes Himself Known to His Brothers

content: How old was Joseph when he was tending the flock with his brothers?
explanation: He brought his father a bad report about his brothers. “When Joseph was seventeen years old, he was tending the flock with his brothers” (Genesis 37:2, BSB)

content: Which brother tried to save Joseph by telling the others to throw him in a pit instead of killing him?
explanation: Reuben planned to bring Joseph back to their father. “Reuben said this so that he could rescue Joseph from their hands and return him to his father.” (Genesis 37:22, BSB)

content: Which brother suggested selling Joseph instead of killing him?
explanation: He said there was no profit in killing their brother. “Then Judah said to his brothers, “What profit will we gain if we kill our brother and cover up his blood?” (Genesis 37:26, BSB)

content: For how much silver did Joseph's brothers sell him?
explanation: The traders took Joseph down to Egypt. “and sold him for twenty shekels of silver” (Genesis 37:28, BSB)

content: In Egypt, who bought Joseph from the Ishmaelites?
explanation: Potiphar was an officer of Pharaoh. “an Egyptian named Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh and captain of the guard, bought him” (Genesis 39:1, BSB)

content: Why did Joseph succeed while serving in Potiphar's house?
explanation: Potiphar put him in charge of everything he owned. “And the LORD was with Joseph, and he became a successful man” (Genesis 39:2, BSB)

content: When Potiphar's wife grabbed Joseph by his cloak, what did Joseph do?
options: Left the cloak and ran outside
explanation: Joseph refused to sin against God. “But leaving his cloak in her hand, he escaped and ran outside.” (Genesis 39:12, BSB)

content: While Joseph was in prison, what did the warden put him in charge of?
explanation: The LORD gave Joseph success even in prison. “And the warden put all the prisoners under Joseph’s care” (Genesis 39:22, BSB)

content: Which two officers of Pharaoh ended up in prison with Joseph?
options: The chief cupbearer and chief baker
The chief priest and a scribe
explanation: Pharaoh was angry with them. “the chief cupbearer and the chief baker” (Genesis 40:2, BSB)

content: In prison, Joseph said the three branches in the cupbearer's dream meant what?
explanation: In three days the cupbearer got his job back. “The three branches are three days.” (Genesis 40:12, BSB)

content: After the cupbearer was set free from prison, what did he do about Joseph?
explanation: Joseph stayed in prison two more years. “The chief cupbearer, however, did not remember Joseph; he forgot all about him.” (Genesis 40:23, BSB)

content: In Pharaoh's second dream, what had scorched the thin heads of grain?
explanation: The thin heads swallowed the plump ones. “thin and scorched by the east wind.” (Genesis 41:6, BSB)

content: How old was Joseph when he entered Pharaoh's service?
explanation: Thirteen years had passed since he was sold. “Now Joseph was thirty years old when he entered the service of Pharaoh king of Egypt.” (Genesis 41:46, BSB)

content: What did Joseph name his firstborn son in Egypt?
explanation: Joseph said God had made him forget his hardship. “Joseph named the firstborn Manasseh” (Genesis 41:51, BSB)

content: During the famine, how many of Joseph's brothers first went to Egypt to buy grain?
explanation: Benjamin stayed home with Jacob. “So ten of Joseph’s brothers went down to buy grain from Egypt.” (Genesis 42:3, BSB)

content: Which brother did Jacob keep at home when the others first went to Egypt for grain?
explanation: Jacob was afraid harm might come to him. “But Jacob did not send Joseph’s brother Benjamin with his brothers” (Genesis 42:4, BSB)

content: When Joseph's brothers came to Egypt to buy grain, did they recognize him?
explanation: Joseph recognized them, but he looked like an Egyptian ruler. “Although Joseph recognized his brothers, they did not recognize him.” (Genesis 42:8, BSB)

content: Which of his brothers did Joseph keep bound in Egypt?
explanation: The others had to go home and bring Benjamin. “he took Simeon from them and had him bound before their eyes.” (Genesis 42:24, BSB)

content: Whose grain sack did Joseph order his silver cup to be hidden in?
explanation: The youngest brother was Benjamin. “Put my cup, the silver one, in the mouth of the youngest one’s sack” (Genesis 44:2, BSB)

content: At the end of Genesis, what did Joseph tell his brothers about the evil they had planned against him?
explanation: God used it to save many lives. “As for you, what you intended against me for evil, God intended for good” (Genesis 50:20, BSB)

content: When Jacob came down to Egypt, what did Joseph do when he met his father?
explanation: Father and son were together again after many years. “Joseph presented himself to him, embraced him, and wept profusely.” (Genesis 46:29, BSB)

content: When Joseph was sold, what were the traders' camels carrying down to Egypt?
explanation: The caravan was coming from Gilead. “Their camels were carrying spices, balm, and myrrh on their way down to Egypt.” (Genesis 37:25, BSB)

content: What was Potiphar's position in Egypt?
explanation: He was an officer of Pharaoh. “an officer of Pharaoh and captain of the guard.” (Genesis 37:36, BSB)

content: In the chief baker's dream in prison, how many baskets were on his head?
explanation: Joseph said the three baskets were three days. “There were three baskets of white bread on my head.” (Genesis 40:16, BSB)

content: On what occasion were Pharaoh's cupbearer and baker brought out of prison?
explanation: Pharaoh held a feast for all his officials. “On the third day, which was Pharaoh’s birthday” (Genesis 40:20, BSB)

content: How long after the cupbearer's release did Pharaoh have his troubling dream?
explanation: Then the cupbearer finally remembered Joseph. “After two full years had passed, Pharaoh had a dream” (Genesis 41:1, BSB)

content: What Egyptian name did Pharaoh give Joseph?
explanation: Joseph took charge of all the land of Egypt. “Pharaoh gave Joseph the name Zaphenath-paneah” (Genesis 41:45, BSB)

content: Whom did Pharaoh give Joseph as his wife?
explanation: Her father was priest of On. “and he gave him Asenath daughter of Potiphera, priest of On, to be his wife.” (Genesis 41:45, BSB)

content: What did Joseph name his second son in Egypt?
explanation: Joseph said God had made him fruitful. “And the second son he named Ephraim” (Genesis 41:52, BSB)

content: When Jacob met Pharaoh in Egypt, how old did he say he was?
explanation: Jacob said his years had been few and hard. ““My travels have lasted 130 years,” Jacob replied.” (Genesis 47:9, BSB)

content: How old was Jacob when his life ended in Egypt?
explanation: He lived seventeen years in Egypt. “and the length of his life was 147 years.” (Genesis 47:28, BSB)

content: How old was Joseph when he died in Egypt?
explanation: His body was placed in a coffin in Egypt. “So Joseph died at the age of 110.” (Genesis 50:26, BSB)

content: In Jacob's blessing of his sons, from which son would the scepter not depart?
explanation: Kings would come from Judah's line. “The scepter will not depart from Judah” (Genesis 49:10, BSB)

content: When Joseph rode in Pharaoh's second chariot, what did men call out before him?
explanation: Joseph was placed over all Egypt. “with men calling out before him, “Bow the knee!”” (Genesis 41:43, BSB)
